subject: BlueArc partnership: certification manifest & test plan
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Uma Patel <uma.patel@bluearc.com>, eng-sales@bluearc.com
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 9 Mar 2027 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: BlueArc partnership: certification manifest & test plan

Hi Uma,

Thanks again for taking the call yesterday. Per our discussion, I'm attaching Redwood's initial certification checklist for ISV reference deployments (redwood-cert-checklist-v1.xlsx). It's a lightweight manifest we use to validate reference solutions against our production serving runtime and security baseline.

High-level asks to progress to a partner 'certified' badge:
- Provide a network topology diagram that shows inbound/outbound flows for your connector/service to Redwood (we can review NAT/firewall and VPC peering options).
- Share sandbox access (service account or ephemeral creds) with a read-only role so our validation team can run end-to-end inference tests.
- List the image/container tags and the model packaging format you plan to use.

Proposed next steps: if you can share the topology + sandbox access by end of week (Fri 12th), we can schedule a 3-day validation window (Mon-Wed 15-17 Mar) and provide a pass/fail artifact and remediation guidance.

Attachments: redwood-cert-checklist-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Best,
Markus Klein
Director, Partner Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: Uma Patel <uma.patel@bluearc.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: eng-sales@bluearc.com
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: BlueArc partnership: certification manifest & test plan

Hi Markus —

Thanks for the checklist. We're on board with the timeline. Attaching the network topology diagram (network-topology-diagram.png) and an internal security note describing our public endpoints and allowed CIDR ranges.

Quick clarifications:
- We prefer to run the connector as a managed container in our EKS cluster; images will be provided from our private ECR. Are you able to pull images via a short-lived presigned token, or do you need us to push sampled images to a Redwood registry?
- Sandbox access: we can create a read-only service account and issue a key. Will that be sufficient for your tests?

We'll upload the images to a staging registry if that eases the process; want to avoid opening broader network access.

Regards,
Uma Patel
Head of Partnerships
BlueArc Solutions

Attachments: network-topology-diagram.png (image)
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Uma Patel <uma.patel@bluearc.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: BlueArc partnership: certification manifest & test plan

Uma — thanks for the diagram, that helps.

Short answers from the infra side:
- Presigned pull tokens for your ECR are fine. If you can provide temp creds scoped to the image pull and a single repo, we'll use those during the validation window.
- Service account key is also fine for sandbox tests; please scope it to read-only and include the accepted IP ranges. If you can send the key as a PEM file or a one-time download link, attach it to a secure transfer (we can also accept a password-protected file via the Drive link).

I've attached a short access manifest (poc-sandbox-access.txt) template you can fill out with usernames, token expiry, and registry names — this will speed our onboarding.

Two technical requests to include in the manifest:
1) A sample inference payload (JSON) and expected approximate latency/throughput numbers so we can size batching and KV cache tests.
2) Any SAML/OIDC metadata if you plan to exercise SSO in the private deploy flow.

Thanks — we'll prepare the validation harness once we have the access details.

— Priyom
Senior SWE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachments: poc-sandbox-access.txt (text)
From: Evan Chu <evan.chu@ecosys.io>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Uma Patel <uma.patel@bluearc.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 08:41:00 -0700
Subject: Re: BlueArc partnership: certification manifest & test plan

Hi Priyom / Markus —

Evan from Ecosys (we run BlueArc's staging registry) here. Quick note on the registery and access.

We can provide short-lived tokens for image pull; I'll create a role-scoped token valid for 72 hours and share it to the manifest you provided. Also attaching SAML metadata (we'll provide the entityID) if Redwood needs to test SSO-based workflows.

Timeline: tokens ready by EOD today. One ask from BlueArc: they want a light smoke validation that exercises the model with 100 concurrent users and confirms fallback behavior on simulated latency spikes. Can Redwood confirm those acceptance criteria and whether they count as 'passing' the certification?

Thanks,
Evan Chu
Platform Ops, Ecosys
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Uma Patel <uma.patel@bluearc.com>, Evan Chu <evan.chu@ecosys.io>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 16:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: BlueArc partnership: certification manifest & test plan

Uma / Evan —

Great — thanks for the quick turnaround. Confirming next steps and acceptance criteria so everyone's aligned:

1) Access: Ecosys will provide registry pull token (72h) and BlueArc will provide the read-only service account key scoped to our sandbox CIDR. Priyom, we'll use the poc-sandbox-access.txt as the single source of truth for secrets and expiry.

2) Validation window: Redwood will run a 3-day validation: Mon 15 Mar — Wed 17 Mar (PST). We'll execute:
   - Functional tests: end-to-end inference against supplied payloads
   - Performance smoke: 100 concurrent users, observe latency P50/P95 and confirm correct KV-cache behavior
   - Resilience: simulate 250–750ms added network latency to upstreams and confirm graceful fallback to model variants

3) Passing criteria: all functional tests green, P95 latency under 850ms for nominal payloads, and automatic fallback triggers on simulated latency (we'll provide logs + a remediation checklist). If anything fails, we'll produce a remediation plan for BlueArc and certify once fixes are validated.

4) Deliverables: post-validation report + signed certification badge asset and a short README for the reference deployment.

Uma — please confirm you can provide the token + service account key by EOD today and the sample payloads by Monday morning. We'll schedule a brief kickoff (30m) on Monday 15th first thing to align runbooks.

Thanks — looking forward to this.

Laura Bennett
Sr. Product Manager, Integrations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-cert-checklist-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)
